_note: A5 §16 — the first known-answer suite, for the CLOSE profile only. Every expected finding names GOVERNED HANDLES from the seeded ledger (accounts, entities, reconciliation ids), never words a model might choose. `why` records where each known answer comes from, so a later reader can check it rather than trust it.

scenarios.title: June controller review
scenarios.objective: Review the June close, identify the material unresolved issues, and prepare a concise controller briefing with traceable evidence.

expectedFindings.label: MDH intercompany receivable does not tie to the foreign OpCos' payables
expectedFindings.why: Phase 3A recorded this as a genuine derived finding: MDH's intercompany receivable is $6.18M above the foreign OpCos' payables, and it is the one material unresolved item in the June close.

expectedFindings.label: material close blockers remain
expectedFindings.why: closeBlockers() derives these from the checklist, reconciliation and flux records; the run must surface them rather than report readiness alone.

expectedAbsences.label: FY2025 figures
expectedAbsences.why: FY2025 is not in the governed ledger. A run that states a FY2025 figure has invented one.

expectedFindings.label: the JD Edwards APAC source is unavailable
expectedFindings.why: SOURCE_HEALTH declares jde UNAVAILABLE. A source system is not an account or a fact, so there is no governed handle to match on — this is the case §5 admits a word match for, and the word is the system's own name.
